scanned.prior_coverage: Previous selections used the first 98 posts plus six style references already locked as shallow-precise, dark-command, and soft-system. This batch looked beyond that set, using only already saved local text and media URLs.
scanned.note: This is not a full inventory of the 811 saved posts. Post created_at is not a like timestamp. Same-source repeats were not counted as extra items.

refero.action: Did not retry live Refero style IDs and did not invent any. Direction locks come from actually read public stills, author text, and typography/color/anti-slop craft rules.

rejected_after_view_summary: A sage-tinted dashboard theme was rejected as a color reskin of a conventional light admin, not a new style.
Two light product/marketing workbench stills were too close to shallow-precise, or were pricing/modal marketing frames, not a new workbench language.

A polished light analytics window on an atmospheric field overlapped existing floating-shell plus light dashboard patterns; later collage pages in the same post were multi-product galleries and cannot lock a style.
A mobile wallet product was not used as a workbench style, because transferring it would change the shared task product.

axes.visual_style: Layout rhythm, density, morphology, color roles, and typographic material. Not a swatch swap.
axes.layout: Primary/secondary organization of the same product: list-detail, board-detail, reading-split, calendar-agenda, faceted-table.
axes.typography: Type scale, measure, metadata hierarchy, and reflow. Combinable with style and layout; not a fourth product.
axes.capability: Real, extractable interaction rules such as faceted filters. Not mixed up with style names.
axes.scenario: This batch remains the task workbench. A second shared scenario may be proposed later; it is not required for this implementation round.

items.primary_use: Primary lock for editorial-sheet, and source for the typography module (display vs body vs meta, measure, hairline sectioning, quote rules).
visible_structure: Ivory/cream paper canvas with hairline rules instead of admin cards.
Masthead with small tracked meta (author, date, reading time) and a large high-contrast display title.
Body set to a readable measure, not edge-to-edge.
Numbered section titles, left-ruled block quotes, photo plus caption in a reading column.
items.borrow: Typographic hierarchy, paper field, hairlines, controlled measure, section rhythm.
items.do_not_copy: Article text, person photography, masthead labels tied to that article, or the reading-page product itself.
observation_limits: These stills are long-form reading pages, not a task workbench. Transfer typography and sectioning, do not turn the shared benchmark into a magazine.
Photography is part of the source pages; the workbench has no photo assets and must not fake portraits. Use typography and rules, not stock faces.
Motion was not reviewed; no animation claims.

items.primary_use: Primary lock for amber-ledger, using still 1. Still 2 is only a density/accent boundary, not a product to reproduce.
visible_structure: Still 1: warm-black canvas, gold/amber hairline grid, terse text tabs, dense numeric tables, a sharp magenta accent used on key amounts, small tabular figures.
Still 2: a tiled multi-window desktop with the same amber accent and dense monitors, plus decorative and branded elements.
items.borrow: From still 1 only: instrument density, hairline partitions, typographic numbers, scarce sharp accent for key values, text-like navigation.
items.do_not_copy: Product name, wordmark, model names, cost figures, pixel-game window, wallpaper, or a window-manager OS shell.
observation_limits: Still 2 must not be used to turn the workbench into a desktop of floating app windows.
Do not replace the 10 tasks with token-cost or model metrics to make the style look denser.

items.primary_use: Primary evidence for the calendar-agenda layout module. Not a new visual style.
visible_structure: Period chips for months, with one period filled/selected.
Week-row agenda: numbered week gutter, event tiles in the row, empty and weekend rows labeled.
Still 2 adds a side month grid plus an upcoming list, while keeping the same agenda as the primary column.
items.borrow: Period chips, week-row agenda, optional side month grid and upcoming list, empty-row labeling.
items.do_not_copy: School/exam copy, class numbers, pastel tile colors as a required style, avatar, or product chrome. Pastel event color is not the layout rule.
observation_limits: The source is an exam calendar, not the shared task product. Only the organization pattern transfers.
A caption under the Exams heading refers to attendance; that inconsistency must not be copied.
No reviewed mobile reflow still in this post. Narrow-screen stacking is an acceptance rule, not an observed animation.

items.primary_use: Primary structural evidence for reading-split (nav | list | reading pane), plus typographic/alignment anti-patterns from the author's on-image critique.
visible_structure: Three clear columns: folder/account nav, message index, typographic reading pane with a meeting header and long body.

Author annotations mark: clipped or overflowing chrome, labels cut off, icons visually larger or taller than text, same control style used for different meanings, regions without a divider, clipped shadow.
items.borrow: Three-pane primary/secondary reading split; keep regions separated; keep label text fully visible; icons must not overpower text; do not use one control skin for two meanings without a second cue.
items.do_not_copy: Mail product IA (compose, promotional tabs, provider lists), message content, or the red critique markup.
observation_limits: This is a critique still, not a finished style lock. Use it for structure and failure modes.
The source scenario is mail. The shared implementation stays a task workbench.

items.primary_use: Evidence for a denser tabular organization and for the facet-query-filter capability. Not a new visual style.
visible_structure: Left facet column with counts, checkboxes, date and range controls.
Top query/search field, reset, and a result-count line.
A compact distribution strip above a dense table; one expanded row showing extra fields; typographic status values.
items.borrow: Faceted filters with counts, visible result count, dense table as a list alternative, optional structured search tokens in addition to plain text.
items.do_not_copy: Log rows, hosts, latency bars, brands, or a 2.9k-row histogram. Any distribution in our product must be computed from the 10 benchmark tasks only.
observation_limits: Author text mentions a command palette and URL state; the palette itself is not visible in this still. A command palette is optional and must not invent unreviewed timings.
This is an observability table, not the shared task product.
Motion and infinite scroll were not reviewed.

items.primary_use: Secondary support for editorial-sheet and for treating the detail pane as a typographic document with labeled status. Not a third style, and not a complete IA lock.
visible_structure: Marketing collage on a sage field: profile list, typographic invoice document, styling panel, status chips with icons and short names, document export still.
items.borrow: Detail-as-document (title, meta rows, tabular figures), status as short name plus icon, paper-like reading surface.
items.do_not_copy: Brand, invoice copy, sage marketing collage composition, or decorative 3D seal as a required motif.
observation_limits: This is a feature collage, not one complete workbench information architecture.
Sage fill and window chrome are supporting clues, not enough alone to justify a separate style.

layouts.implement_this_round: optional-as-layout-or-as-list-density; prefer capability first if capacity is tight

typography_modules.note: This is typography, not a visual style and not a component pack. It can be combined with any implemented style and layout.
